skill.name: audit-before-i-publish
skill.description: Review a finished social post for claims, consent, structure, ending, and author voice. Rank up to three fixes and assess publication readiness.
skill.summary: Audit a finished post and prioritize the changes that matter before publication.
skill.author: prateeks367

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 90 uses Markdown backticks to format get_voice_profile in a prose description of an optional connector. There is no Ruby or shell execution.
Line 92 formats score_voice_match as inline Markdown while explaining optional voice scoring. The text contains no executable command or command substitution.
Line 95 describes improve_post as an optional editing tool, with Markdown formatting rather than executable backticks. No shell invocation is present.
Lines 97 to 98 describe publish_post behind a preview and one-time confirmation. The backticks mark a tool name, not shell execution or unauthorized publication.
Lines 32 to 33 ask whether an anecdote belongs to the author and happened as written. This is editorial authenticity checking, not system reconnaissance.
Lines 37 to 38 ask whether identifiable colleagues or clients consented to appearing in a post. This protects privacy and requests no system information.

content.value_statement: Finished posts can contain unsupported claims, privacy concerns, or unclear structure. This skill reviews the draft and ranks up to three fixes before publication.
actual_capabilities: Review the first line and visible opening for reader interest.
Flag unsupported numbers, questionable anecdotes, unfulfilled promises, and consent concerns.
Check whether the post follows one idea with useful paragraphs and readable line breaks.
Classify the ending and recommend changes only when a specific problem exists.
Identify specific lines that appear inconsistent with the author's voice.
Rank at most three fixes, report checks that passed, and state whether the draft is ready.
limitations: Requires an existing draft and does not write posts from nothing.
Does not predict reach, engagement, or publication performance.
Cannot establish factual accuracy or consent without supporting evidence from the author.
Provides no numerical voice score alone; optional VoiceMOAT features require a connector and a Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Review a Professional Post
use_cases.description: Check a finished LinkedIn post for unsupported claims, a weak opening, and unnecessary paragraphs before sharing it.

use_cases.title: Check a Client Story
use_cases.description: Review a customer anecdote for attribution, identifiable details, consent concerns, and promises the draft does not support.

use_cases.title: Preserve a Personal Voice
use_cases.description: Compare a finished draft with supplied writing examples and identify specific lines that sound inconsistent with the author.

prompt_templates.title: Check Publication Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this finished post: [draft]. Say whether you would publish it unchanged and give at most three fixes in priority order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a completed draft

prompt_templates.title: Review Claims and Consent
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this draft: [draft]. Review numbers, anecdotes, promises, and identifiable people using this context: [sources and consent details]. Flag missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of factual and privacy concerns

prompt_templates.title: Compare Author Voice
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this draft: [draft]. Compare its voice with these posts: [writing samples]. Identify specific mismatched lines without assigning a numerical score.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Complete Editorial Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this LinkedIn draft: [draft], using [sources], [consent context], and [voice samples]. Review each step, rank up to three fixes, and report clean checks. Do not rewrite the whole post or publish it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with evidence and clear action boundaries

output_examples.input: Review a finished post containing an unsourced growth figure, an identifiable customer, and a generic closing question.
output: First: Source or remove the growth figure.
Second: Confirm customer consent or remove identifying details.
Third: Remove the closing question unless it invites a specific, relevant response.
Clean checks: The draft follows one idea and uses readable line breaks.

output_examples.input: Review a focused post with an attributed statistic, no identifiable third parties, and a direct ending.
output: Clean checks: The opening matches the body, the statistic is attributed, and the ending adds no unnecessary prompt.
Voice assessment remains qualitative without a connected profile.

best_practices: Provide the complete draft, intended platform, and sources for numerical claims.
Include consent context for identifiable people and writing samples for voice comparison.
Address the highest-priority issue first and retain passages that passed the review.
anti_patterns: Use the audit to generate a post from nothing.
Request guaranteed engagement or a numerical voice score without a connected profile.
Rewrite the entire draft when one targeted change resolves the issue.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a finished draft. Include sources, consent details, and writing samples when they are relevant.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my entire post?
faq.answer: The skill prioritizes targeted fixes rather than complete rewrites. It returns at most three recommended changes.

faq.question: Can it approve a draft without changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend publishing the draft unchanged and identify checks that passed.

faq.question: Does it predict how a post will perform?
faq.answer: No. It reviews publication readiness, not future reach or engagement.

faq.question: Does it verify every claim independently?
faq.answer: It asks whether claims have sources and flags missing evidence. The skill includes no independent fact-checking service.

faq.question: What changes with VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: The documentation describes optional voice profiles, voice scoring, deeper editing, and publishing with preview and confirmation. These require a connector and Pro or Enterprise.
